newsitem.title: UGANDA: British Minister supports African efforts for peace.
newsitem.headline: British Minister supports African efforts for peace.

text.p: British Minister of State for Foreign and Commonwealth Affairs Tony Lloyd said in Kampala on Sunday that Britain supported the efforts of regional African states to restore peace in the Great Lakes region.

Addressing a news conference after a two-day visit to Uganda, during which he met President Yoweri Museveni and other leaders, he said their talks had covered regional security, stability and econmomic affairs.

The United Kingdom did not seek direct involvement in the efforts of African regional states to restore constitutional rule in Burundi after last year's military coup there, Lloyd said. But he commended those efforts under the chairmanship of former Tanzanian president and African elder statesman Julius Nyerere.

Lloyd said he supported Museveni's call to the Sudan government to endeavour to secure the release of 34 Ugandan schoolgirls who had been abducted into Sudan by a Ugandan rebel group, the Lord's Resistance Army, operating in northern Uganda.
